report.summary: Reviewed chunk 23 of 25 of daedalus/spine/picker.py: function _build_packet (lines 2641-2746). No public symbols, claims verified.

handoff.purpose: Build human review packet for candidate attempt, including rationale, diff display, and next steps.

claims.text: The patch bytes are decoded for display only. A human promoting this must write artifact_path (the raw bytes) -- a diff round-tripped through a terminal is not the artifact that was hashed and gated.
claims.why: The code prints the diff text for display and later references artifact_path for the raw bytes. It warns that the displayed diff is not the hashed artifact.

claims.text: NOTHING HAS BEEN APPLIED. This is a proposal.
claims.why: The string is appended to the output as a header line.

claims.text: An empty patch is captured and hashed like any other, but showing it as a diff -- and, worse, offering an apply command for it below -- would let "the runner did nothing" read as "here is a change".
claims.why: The code checks for empty patch and outputs a special message, not a diff, and later omits the apply command for empty patches.

claims.text: Windows PowerShell may expose a CP-1252 stdout even when a verifier emits Unicode progress glyphs such as Vite's check mark. The attempt and ledger are already complete when the review packet is printed, so an encoding
claims.why: The function _console_safe is not fully shown; only the docstring is visible. The claim about encoding behavior cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

observations.what: The chunk contains a function _build_packet that builds a human-readable review packet; it is not exported (name starts with underscore).
The code references artifact.diff and artifact.diff_bytes; the attribute diff_bytes is accessed via getattr with a fallback to artifact.diff.
The chunk ends mid-sentence in the docstring of _console_safe.
